questions.wording: What is the place of a body?

answers.label: The inner surface of the body that surrounds it
A space, extended in three dimensions, distinct from the body and remaining when the body leaves
The body's own extension (its internal place); its external place is the surface around it or its situation among other bodies

questions.wording: Is there anything, or any space, beyond the world?

answers.label: Only imaginary space: a lack of bodily quantity that the imagination measures as if it were something
Extension, and so matter: the world has no bound we can assign
Nothing: the space of place was created with the world and is equal to it

questions.wording: Could God make an empty space, by taking away the body in it and letting no other in?
names: fr: si Dieu aneantissoit tout l'air d'une chambre

answers.label: Yes: it implies no contradiction, and God is not bound by the laws he set
No space would remain: with nothing between them the surrounding bodies would touch, distance being a mode of extension

questions.wording: How can a body move if every place is full?

answers.label: The bodies in its way give place and fill the place it leaves, so that matter moves in a ring
Motion requires a space, distinct from the bodies, through which they pass

questions.wording: Why does water follow a piston drawn up a pipe, and why does it stop where it does?

answers.label: Nature's flight from the void: bodies move against their own inclination so that no void may be
The weight of the outside air presses the water up

questions.note: Askable of every snapshot; the pump that stops near 32 feet is reported from c. 1640.

questions.wording: Are there real indivisibles in a continuous quantity, such as points that bound and join its parts?

answers.label: Yes: indivisibles that bound and join the parts, though they do not compose it
No: a magnitude is bounded by the absence of further extension, and its parts are joined of themselves
No: only God is actually infinite; a creature is infinite only in potency, without end in succession
Not infinite but indefinite: without limits in some respect only, as matter in its divisibility and the world in its extent

names: la: numerus motus secundum prius et posterius

answers.label: The number or measure of motion according to before and after
An affection of the natural body by which its duration is divided according to the motions of the heavens
The duration of a created thing as the mind measures it: a mode of thinking, not a property of things

questions.wording: Is the present time only an instant, or has it some extent?

answers.label: Only an instant: time exists in the present by its instant, not by a part
It has parts, or some breadth

questions.wording: By what motion is time measured?

answers.label: The daily revolution of the first movable, the one universal time
The motions of the heavenly bodies, chiefly the sun and moon
Any succession, of motions or of thoughts

questions.wording: What kinds of duration are there?

answers.label: Three: eternity (God), aevum (created spirits), time (bodies)
God's duration alone is without succession; every created duration, angels' included, has succession

questions.wording: Could a body move through an empty space, and would it take time?

answers.label: Yes, and not in an instant
Only in an instant
No

questions.wording: What fills the pores of bodies and the spaces that seem empty?

answers.label: A subtler body: air, a subtle matter, or the subtler parts of the body
Nothing: they are empty

questions.wording: Do bodies act by their size, or by something else?

answers.label: Not by their quantity but by their qualities
By size, figure and motion of their parts

questions.wording: Can a demonstration in geometry settle a question about natural bodies?

answers.label: Yes: what geometry shows of extension holds of bodies
No: mathematical principles are foreign to physics and cannot conclude about natural things

Add a boundary note: 'Divisibility, place, void and time: general physics in all four.
